Context Package + Contract Bundle land as the architectural shift the data-retrieval-primitives spike was building toward. RetrievalContextPackage wraps shape-aware retrieval in one envelope with intent / access (user_id scoping) / proof (per-hit provenance) / budget (token cap). ContractBundle declares per-role what each slot needs from which shaped store; assemble_package walks the contract, dispatches to episodic / tree / tabular, returns a complete or incomplete package. Required-slot misses surface in missing_required_slots so the agent gets told what's missing rather than working with silently-incomplete context. Landed. Two atc-retrieval eval fixes:

1. Prefix matching in score_case: a hit anchor matches an expected anchor when (a) they intersect exactly, OR (b) the expected anchor is a path-prefix of a hit anchor on a `.` or `-` boundary. Lets fixtures express parent-section or part-only expected anchors (`5-3`, `97`) without enumerating every leaf — the eval now matches a hit at §97.3 to expected `97`, and §5-3-1 to expected `5-3`. The boundary check prevents `91` from accidentally matching `915`.

2. Empty-expected case handling: scope-redirect fixtures with empty expected_citations get `no_expected=True` on the RetrievalCase and are excluded from aggregate recall denominator + numerator. Eval no longer mis-scores them as hard misses.

Also relocated merge_sibling_clusters from retrieval/contract.py to store/document_tree.py as a canonical entry point (harness-rvnb prep work — both contract orchestrator and eval can reach it without crossing layers). Added a guard inside merge: skip promotion when the parent path has no segment separator (CFR Part numbers like `91`), because the resulting parent has no regex-extractable anchor and the leaves carry the actual content. Eval intentionally does NOT thread auto_merge anymore (it broke leaf-expected fixtures); prefix matching covers parent-expected cases without disrupting leaf retrieval.
